heading: Together ~ we prepare, we journey, we integrate. Care within connection.
safetyCardBody: No needles — the medicine dissolves in your mouth or is a small nasal spray. You rest somewhere comfortable, with music and an eye mask if you like. Becky stays with you the entire time and keeps a quiet eye on how you are doing.
facts: Over fifty years of use in medicine
Relief can come quickly — sometimes the same day
You are never left on your own
Everything is paced to you, never rushed
intro:
Legally prescribed medication 
dissociative medicine
holistic integrative care

Expanded states of consciousness can open the door to profound self-discovery, helping you reconnect with your inner wisdom, meet the different parts of yourself with compassion, and gain fresh perspective on your inner world. When approached with intention and supported through thoughtful integration, these experiences can create space for healing, harmony, and a deeper connection with the many parts of who you are. They can inspire lasting personal growth, emotional well-being, and a greater sense of wholeness, authenticity, and inner alignment.

Some medicines quiet a symptom. This one softens the walls we build over years — and for a little while, makes it possible to see ourselves with fresh eyes. What you do with that opening is where the real change happens.

sections.heading: What this medicine is
paragraphs: More recently, doctors and therapists discovered something else about it: given in small, careful amounts, it can lift the heaviness of depression and anxiety remarkably quickly — often in hours rather than the weeks other medicines take. This use is newer than its original one, and the doctor looking after you will talk that through with you honestly.

sections.heading: Why it helps
paragraphs: When we have hurt for a long time, our thinking wears grooves — the same worries, the same harsh voice, the same story about who we are. Those grooves feel like permanent truth. They aren't.

This medicine gently loosens them. For a few hours, the usual sense of "me" softens and quiets, and something more spacious opens up behind it. People often describe stepping back far enough to finally see their life clearly — sometimes with relief, sometimes with tears, often with a tenderness toward themselves they had not felt in years.

sections.heading: What it feels like
paragraphs: Everyone's experience is their own, but there are common threads: a floating, dreamlike quality; colors and music felt more deeply; time stretching. Your body feels distant and pleasantly heavy. Many people feel a great sense of ease.

With gentler amounts, you can still talk and be talked to — the conversation just goes somewhere more honest than usual. With stronger ones, the experience turns inward, more like a vivid dream you are travelling through.

It usually begins within five or ten minutes, deepens for about half an hour, and eases off over the next hour or so. You'll feel gently tired afterward, and someone you trust will drive you home to rest.

Sometimes what surfaces is hard — grief, or something long avoided. That is not a sign anything has gone wrong. Becky is trained to stay steady with you through exactly those moments, and they are often where the deepest healing lives.

sections.heading: Why the medicine alone isn't enough
paragraphs: The medicine opens a door. It does not walk you through, and it does not do the work for you. What matters is having someone beside you who knows the territory — before, during, and especially afterward.
Just as a body knows how to knit a broken bone, something in us knows how to heal. This work simply clears the way and keeps you company while it happens.

honestNote: Honest note: this is still a newer path, and no one can promise you a particular outcome. It helps many people, it does not help everyone, and it works best as part of a wider circle of care.
metaDescription: A gentle, plain-language introduction to ketamine-assisted therapy — what the medicine is, what the experience feels like, and why it is always paired with real support.
